answers.U2-S1: Trees and plants start getting ready for next spring way earlier than people think, in late summer, when the new buds form.
answers.U2-S2: To show that the new buds really do push the old leaves off the trees, which is how trees lose their leaves in fall.
answers.U2-S3: a description of how some oaks and beeches are weak, indecisive trees that can't make up their minds about dropping their leaves.
answers.U2-S4: A tree needs to be strong and healthy to have enough power to push its leaves off; weak or dead trees can't drop them.
answers.U2-S5: the beginning or start of something
answers.U2-S6: He partly agrees things start early but says the real start is even earlier, in late summer when buds form, not December.
answers.U2-S7: Because buds and catkins have the new growth packed inside them, and they hatch open in spring warmth like eggs do.
answers.U2-S8: Each season produces the next one, like a mother giving birth; the old season creates the new season's buds.
answers.U2-S9: His own observations of trees and plants, like cutting open buds and looking at fallen leaves.
answers.U2-S10: It says that in fall Nature shuts down and closes up, but first she gets everything ready so spring can open again.
